title: An End-to-End Transformer Model for 3D Object Detection

statements: Through extensive experiments, we show 3DETR outperforms the well-established and highly optimized VoteNet baselines on the challenging ScanNetV2 dataset by 9.5%.
Of particular interest, VoteNet [42] casts 3D detection as a set-to-set problem, i.e., transforming an unordered set of inputs (point cloud), into an unordered set of outputs (bounding boxes).
In particular, the recent Transformer [68] based model, called DETR [4], casts 2D object detection as a set-to-set problem.
To that end, we develop 3D DEtection TRansformer (3DETR) a simple to implement 3D detection method that uses fewer hand-coded design decisions and also casts detection as a set-to-set problem.

Inspired by this observation, we ask the following question: can we leverage Transformers to learn a 3D object detector without relying on handdesigned inductive biases?
To that end, we develop 3D DEtection TRansformer (3DETR) a simple to implement 3D detection method that uses fewer hand-coded design decisions and also casts detection as a set-to-set problem.

evidence.quote: Through extensive experiments, we show 3DETR outperforms the well-established and highly optimized VoteNet baselines on the challenging ScanNetV2 dataset by 9.5%.
On two standard indoor 3D detection benchmarks, ScanNetV2 and SUN RGB-D we achieve 65.0% AP and 59.0% AP respectively, outperforming an improved VoteNet baseline by 9.5% AP50 on ScanNetV2.

limitations.summary: Unlike DETR, 3DETR does not employ a ConvNet backbone, and solely relies on Transformers trained from scratch.
items: Unlike DETR, 3DETR does not employ a ConvNet backbone, and solely relies on Transformers trained from scratch.
Our model does not use color information (used for visualization only).
We use positional embeddings in the decoder as it does not have direct access to the coordinates (operates on encoder features and query embeddings).
Compared to PointNet++, 3DETR-m does not rely on multiple layers of 3D feature aggregation and 3D upsampling.
